notes.title: Added options to handle camera mirroring.
notes.content:
Certain cameras such as the one in the Kinect V2 were found to have strange mirroring behavior. I have added two new configuration options to give more control over the mirroring, allowing more flexibility in general, which in turn makes it possible to fix the mirroring behavior of strange cameras.

Camera -> Camera Mirroring
This defaults to true for the old behavior, but if toggled will flip the image horizontally.
Tracking -> Swap Handedness
Defaulted to false for the old behavior, but if toggled it will flip left/right for gesture processing, which is also needed when using a camera with alternate mirroring behavior.

(I also want to add that the depth sensing capabilities of the Kinect V2 are not used in Virtual Touch Screen 2-- I only mention it as an example because it is the only camera I have seen so far which exhibits the alternate mirroring configuration.)

notes.title: Minor Fixes for Advanced Gesture Profiles
notes.content:
Fixed some issues with the Advanced Gesture Profile engine and the default profiles:
[list]
[*]Fixed issue with the advanced gesture profile engine that would allow keys to become stuck in some cases.
[*]Adjusted behavior of the "await" action to always stop waiting when the associated gesture is lost, unless the Continue Processing After Gesture End option is enabled.
[*]Adjusted the Virtual Mouse and Default Point Gestures profiles to fix an issue where the pointer position would be stuck until activating the middle mouse combo for the first time.
[*]Adjusted conditional checks to consider undefined option values to also be considered disabled option values.  To determine the difference between undefined and disabled, an explicit check for undefined is required.
[/list]

notes.title: Translations Update
notes.content: Language translations have been updated to keep them in sync with the current content of the tool.

notes.title: Small Update and Bug Fix
notes.content: I have updated dependencies that may help improve tracking and fixed a rendering bug with the underlay where it would be mostly transparent when underlay background removal is turned on.

notes.title: 50% Off! The base price of Virtual Touch Screen 2 has been reduced to $9.99 USD
notes.content:
Setting a price for a unique product like Virtual Touch Screen 2 has proven to be a nuanced challenge. The customer base mainly comprises two groups: media professionals utilizing it for high-quality content production and the average home user enjoying the functionality and experience.

In an effort to scale the success of Virtual Touch Screen 2, I've reevaluated our pricing strategy. To ensure broad accessibility, the primary focus is now on offering a compelling price for the average home user.

💰 [b]New Base Price:[/b] I'm excited to share that the base price of Virtual Touch Screen 2 is now $9.99 USD, a 50% reduction.

🌍 [b]Consistent Regional Pricing:[/b] Regional pricing has been reduced to match the new base price, effectively phasing out most regional pricing differences.

The goal is to get Virtual Touch Screen 2 into as many hands as possible, fostering a community that allows for continuous improvement. Thank you for your support.

notes.title: Audio Revamp + Virtual Mouse Improvements
notes.content:
[list]
[*] The audio system has been overhauled.  There is a new section in the configuration specifically for sound, allowing independent control of gesture start, end, and interval sounds and their volume levels, with four sound choices included and the ability to select sounds from your file system.  This feature is also now available in the advanced profile editor.
[*] Both the relative version and the absolute version of the virtual mouse now both lock their positions while rolling the mouse wheel to prevent sending mouse wheel events to different windows.
[/list]

notes.title: Small Improvements
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Accidental Pinch Protection and Accidental Point Protection now also control how difficult it is to transition between the two gesture types.  Pinch protection is disabled by default, and with these settings users will no longer get stuck in point mode when trying to pinch.
[*] Added an additional safeguard against the overlay failing to be on top of other windows.  This is a bit of an arms race, as the operating system developers keep making changes to make it more difficult for unfocused programs to display in front of focused programs, but by nature of what Virtual Touch Screen 2 does, the overlay obviously needs to be on top of other programs.
[/list]

notes.title: 11 11 Bug Fix Patch
notes.content:
Today I have some nice fixes that should make the tool a lot easier to use.
[list]
[*] Improved gesture transitioning for different types of pinches, reducing how often unintended gestures are triggered during transitions.
[*] Reduced the chance of unintended gestures while hands are raising or dropping.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Background Removal Share Window would show a doubled image in the background instead of removing it.  This bug was also silently hurting performance in other areas.
[*] Added a second set of green screen removal options.  This can be helpful if you have two different green screens that don't match up perfectly.
[/list]

notes.title: Minor Update
notes.content:
Added the ability to change the appearance of both contact indicators and near indicators.
Added some missing translations.
Application is now configured to not show the Steam overlay, resolving the issue with Steam overlay elements appearing erroneously throughout the UI.

To get the latest update, restarting Steam may be required.

notes.title: November 5th Significant Bug Fixes
notes.content:
Valiant users of Virtual Touch Screen 2, a monumental announcement graces thy realm! Behold, for a dual triumph hath descended upon our domain, marking a momentous chapter in the saga of our software.

Our noble quest to fortify the integrity of Virtual Touch Screen 2 hath borne fruit with the vanquishing of two vexing adversaries. The omission of MSVC, which erstwhile thwarted the aspirations of some valiant users, has been rectified. Furthermore, the unintentional alteration of the camera gain, which marred the visual experience, has been vanquished from our code.

This momentous update not only restores the missing MSVC, allowing all valiant users to partake in the wondrous touch of their virtual screen but also guarantees a steadfast visual journey, free from inadvertent alterations that once vexed the noble voyagers through our software.

Embrace this virtuoso update, where the combined victories pave the path to an unparalleled experience within the realms of Virtual Touch Screen 2. Your virtuous endeavors through hand gestures and webcam sorcery shall now be met with a smoother, visually resplendent, and vastly improved interface.

Take hold of this update, dear users, and revel in the glory of a software reborn—Viva la Virtual Touch Screen 2, now more vibrant, valiant, and victorious than ever before!

(It is the 5th of November so I had to add some pizzazz.  If you don't get it, watch the movie V for Vendetta.)

More plainly:
[olist]
[*] The MSVC redistributable is required for the program to run, but was not included.  For users who did not already have the MSVC 2022 redistributable installed for another program, it would fail to start the Virtual Touch Screen.  With this update, MSVC will now be automatically installed if missing.
[*] The program was erroneously changing the camera gain even when set to leave the camera exposure settings alone.  If you were effected by this, you may need to correct your camera exposure compensation, either by manually changing it in the camera settings or by setting the tool to automatically manage it with the settings in the Camera section, under Camera Exposure Settings Override and Camera Automatic Camera Brightness Override.

To get the latest version of the program, you may need to completely exit and reopen Steam, or more simply restart your computer.
[/olist]
